sections.label: EUSFTA border enforcement measures
sections.summary: After the EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement concluded in 2014, Singapore agreed to add border enforcement measures against goods infringing IP rights.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Following the conclusion of the European Union-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (EUSFTA) in 2014, Singapore agreed to add new border enforcement measures to deal with goods infringing various IP rights.

sections.label: Customs seizure powers expanded
sections.summary: The Bill lets Customs seize, on right holders' request, suspected infringing exports and suspected infringing registered design imports or exports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendments in the Bill will now allow Customs to seize, on the right holders’ request, (a) goods which are suspected of infringing copyright or trade marks that are to be exported, and (b) goods which are suspected of infringing registered designs that are imported or are to be exported.

sections.label: Information disclosure to right holders
sections.summary: Providing information to right holders is a narrow exception to Customs' confidentiality obligations under the Customs Act and Regulation of Imports and Exports Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The power to provide information to right holders will be a narrow exception to Customs’ obligations to keep any information obtained under the Customs Act and the Regulation of Imports and Exports Act confidential.

sections.label: Three-stage implementation of measures
sections.summary: The Bill's changes and the GI Act's border measures will be implemented in three stages for Customs' needs, business adaptation and EUSFTA obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The changes sought under this Bill, together with the enhanced border enforcement measures under the GI Act passed already in April 2014, will be implemented in three stages to meet Customs’ operational needs, provide businesses with sufficient time to adapt and also correspond with our obligations under the EUSFTA, which is in the process of being ratified.

sections.label: Detention scope and abuse safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill expands detention to exports, allows right holders to initiate it, and requires compensation if no infringement action follows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Detention is important because the protection of the intangible IP right rests in the tangible goods which bear the IP right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill expands the scope of the power to detain to include, not just the import, but also the export of copies of alleged infringing goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, detention can be initiated by the IP right holder and not just a state official.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To prevent abuse, a balance has been struck by getting the requestor to pay compensation for loss or damage as a result of the seizure if the requestor requests to detain the suspected infringing goods but did not institute any infringement action in the end.

sections.label: Phased implementation of EUSFTA obligations
sections.summary: The Bill implements EUSFTA obligations and will be implemented in phases, as indicated in the press release and reflected in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, to what extent is this provision meant to operate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill, which implements our obligations under the EUSFTA, will be implemented in phases, as indicated in the press release and reflected in the Bill.

sections.label: Bill supports IP border enforcement
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill because it honours international obligations and strengthens border enforcement of IP rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In relation to this, why is it that the distinction between goods in transit that are consigned and those that are not consigned is not drawn for the Geographical Indicators Act and Registered Designs Act at clauses 47 and 53 but are drawn for the Copyright Act and Trade Marks Act at clauses 7, 25, 60 and 78?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Because costs involved in exports and imports have tended to decrease and exported and imported goods have become more widely available, this Bill plays an important role in enhancing our border enforcement of intellectual property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Besides enhancing our border enforcement of IP rights, this Bill helps us honour our obligations under EUSFTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, international agreements are particularly important in IP law because of the principle of territoriality which states that “IP rights granted and recognised in one country are protected within the territory of that country only.” In an increasingly interconnected world and globalised market, the importance of international agreements is heightened further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, Mr Speaker, because of these two broad reasons, first, this Bill honours our international obligations, and second, it strengthens the enforcement of IP rights across our border, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill, which also runs in tandem with the Copyright Act, the Geographical Indications Act 2014, the Registered Design Act and the Trade Marks Act, is timely and in accordance with our obligation under the proposed FTA between the EU and Singapore.

sections.label: Value of IP rights
sections.summary: Inventions, artistic works and brands are meaningless without IP rights, and income per capita is estimated 13 times greater in countries with strong IP protections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, inventions, artistic works and brands are meaningless and determined to have no value without IP rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is estimated that income per capita to be 13 times greater in countries with strong IP protections than those with weak protections.

sections.label: Seizure of exported infringing goods
sections.summary: Under EUSFTA, upon request by the IPR holder, suspected infringing exported goods may be seized under the Copyright Act and Trade Marks Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Pursuant to the EUSFTA obligation, it is my understating that upon request by the IP Right (IPR) holder, it is allowed to seize suspected infringing goods that are exported under the Copyright Act and Trade Marks Act, as stipulated in clause 12 section 140B of the Copyright Act and clause 65 section 82 of Trade Marks Act.

sections.label: Officers' power to require information
sections.summary: Amendments to four IP Acts give authorised officers power to require information or documents for three stated purposes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Otherwise, there may be contrasting issues that arise and can be challenging to resolve, I feel.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Also, as it is being implemented in phases, how is the practical execution going to be done and what is the proposed timeline?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Amendments to the four IP Acts provide authorised officers or senior authorised officers the power to require a person to provide information or documents for three purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, to satisfy a request for information; two, to enable actions to be taken relating to future shipments of goods; and three, for statistical or research purposes.

sections.label: IPSA concerns on retained goods
sections.summary: The IP Students' Association raised concerns on retention of allegedly infringing goods after seizure and detention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The IP Students’ Association (IPSA), comprising law students in both the National University of Singapore and Singapore Management University, raised a number of concerns on the retention of allegedly infringing goods after their seizure and detention.

sections.label: IPSA Indication review recommendation
sections.summary: IPSA recommended an "Indication" review process where a committee or IPOS tribunal expedites evaluation of whether goods are infringing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One recommendation suggested by IPSA would be to have a review process called an “Indication” where a committee or the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) tribunal has an expedited process for evaluating if the goods are, indeed, infringing.

sections.label: EUSFTA counterfeit trademark goods definition
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State is asked to clarify the rationale for deviating from the EUSFTA definition of counterfeit trademark goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify the rationale for deviating from the EUSFTA definition of counterfeit trademark goods?

sections.label: Transit goods detention and port efficiency
sections.summary: Customs generally does not detain goods in transit to keep ports efficient, but may detain suspected infringing goods consigned to a local party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In addition, enforcement actions have to be balanced against the need to maintain our port efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, generally, for goods in transit, Customs officers do not detain the goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This then allows for effective enforcement to be undertaken in the destination country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, as part of our existing international obligations, for suspected copyright infringing copies or counterfeit trade mark goods in transit which are consigned to a local party, Customs officers have the power to initiate ex officio action to detain such goods, because there is a local consignee.

sections.label: Article 10.50 border enforcement approaches
sections.summary: Article 10.50 requires customs authorities to adopt approaches to identify certain counterfeit and pirated goods, with no obligation for patent infringing goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Article 10.50 provides that "the customs authorities shall adopt a range of approaches to identify shipments containing counterfeit trademark goods, pirated copyright goods, pirated design goods, and counterfeit geographical indication goods".

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is no obligation, under this Article, to implement border enforcement measures for patent infringing goods.

sections.label: Travellers' luggage IP rights detention
sections.summary: Goods in travellers' personal luggage may be detained if suspected of infringing IP rights and right holders are prepared to act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Therefore, in such a situation, they would not be detained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, goods in travellers’ personal luggage may be detained if they are suspected of infringing IP rights and right holders are prepared to take action.

sections.label: Court order within three weeks
sections.summary: Within three weeks of instituting an infringement action, IPR holders must obtain a Court order to prevent release of the goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Within three weeks of instituting an infringement action, IPR holders will need to obtain a Court order to prevent the release of the goods.

sections.label: Court orders on destruction and compensation
sections.summary: If the infringement action succeeds the Court may order destruction of goods; if it fails, the Court may order compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Where the infringement action succeeds, the Court may then, as part of the order, also order that the goods to be destroyed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, where the infringement action fails or is dismissed or is discontinued, the Court may order that the IPR holder pay compensation to the defendant.

sections.label: No complaints of IPR abuse
sections.summary: No complaints have been received of IPR holders abusing border enforcement measures, and civil action compensation requests are not tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think it is a question quite rightly asked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We do not track the requests for compensation via civil actions under this mechanism, but the Member will be assured to know that, to date, we have not received any complaints of IPR holders abusing our border enforcement measures, given this mechanism and the other safeguards, such as the need to provide a security deposit, before the goods are seized.

sections.label: Singapore and TRIPS border measures
sections.summary: Singapore is part of the TRIPS Agreement, which requires all WTO countries to have border enforcement measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Singapore is also part of the Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) Agreement, where all WTO countries are required to put in place border enforcement measures.

sections.label: New information powers not EUSFTA
sections.summary: New powers for requesting and providing information are not implemented under EUSFTA obligations but complement Customs' border enforcement duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Member, Mr Azmoon Ahmad, asked for clarification on why the new powers for requesting and providing information are being implemented now and were not implemented before and whether they are related to the EUSFTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These new powers are not implemented pursuant to our EUSFTA obligations but are intended to complement Customs’ border enforcement duties.

sections.label: Customs information for infringement actions
sections.summary: Customs may ask for information relevant to border enforcement, including giving IPR holders names and contact details for infringement actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To be clear, Customs will only be empowered to ask for any information that is relevant to border enforcement for the three defined purposes, and they are very clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, to provide IPR holders with the name and contact details of any person connected with the import or export of the seized goods, where necessary, for instituting infringement actions.

sections.label: Penalty for disclosing information
sections.summary: Anyone who discloses or uses the information for other purposes is guilty of an offence, liable to a fine or imprisonment or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In addition, as provided in the Bill, any person who discloses or uses the information for any other purposes shall be guilty of an offence and be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $6,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.

sections.label: Answer on self-incrimination
sections.summary: The short answer is yes, even if the information may not ultimately turn out to be self-incriminating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The short answer is yes, even if the information may not turn out to be self-incriminating ultimately.

sections.label: Self-incrimination privilege statement admissibility
sections.summary: A self-incriminating statement claimed under privilege cannot be admitted against the person in criminal proceedings for any offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Where a person claims that his statement is self-incriminating and claims the privilege, the statement then cannot be admitted against him in criminal proceedings for any offences.

sections.label: Registered designs border enforcement measures
sections.summary: New border enforcement measures for registered designs will be effected within three years after the EUSFTA enters into force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new border enforcement measures for registered designs will be effected within three years after the EUSFTA enters into force.
